description: Webhook event types emitted by LumiBase v0.1. Every event has a stable envelope (id, type, createdAt, data). Event IDs are globally unique and are the canonical identifier consumers should use for idempotency.

id.description: Globally unique event identifier. Consumers MUST use this field for deduplication.

type.description: The event type key from the types map below.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of event creation.

data.description: Type-specific payload. Fields listed per type below; shapes refer to the payment object described in specs/payments/payment.json.

payment.created.description: A new payment request was created.

payment.processing.description: A transaction hash was submitted and verification has begun.

payment.confirmed.description: Verification succeeded and the payment is confirmed.

payment.failed.description: Reserved for v0.2+. Not emitted in v0.1 because failed is unreachable through the v0.1 confirm endpoint. Included here so consumers and implementers have a stable event shape for when failed becomes reachable.

payment.expired.description: The payment request expired without successful completion. Terminal.

payment.underpaid.description: A valid payment was received but the amount was less than required. Terminal.

payment.overpaid.description: A valid payment was received but the amount was more than required. Terminal.

notes: v0.1 does not emit a payment.cancelled event. Cancellation is initiated by the application, so the canceller already knows.
Events MUST be persisted before any webhook delivery is attempted.
Webhook consumers MUST be idempotent and use the event id field for deduplication.
Delivery retries use exponential backoff; consumers may observe duplicate deliveries of the same event id.
